relationships.history: His supervisor, young enough to be his son, and a good one. Hamid has told him so exactly once.
His neighbour across the landing. He leaves her leftovers; she fixes his phone.
She wants to write about the interpreters. He has said no twice, kindly.

memories.info: The flight out of Kabul with his wife and daughters, and his brother not on it.

profile.tagline: Eleven years translating for an army. Now he translates the register for new arrivals.

appearance.face: a trimmed salt-and-pepper beard, a careful smile
appearance.style: Greenleaf's green apron over a pressed white shirt, grey slacks, polished black shoes
appearance.jewelry: a silver ring with a blue stone, reading glasses on a cord
appearance.silhouette: a lean man in a green apron standing very straight
key_features: Pressed white shirt under a green apron
Silver ring with a blue stone

profile.family_background: Born in Kabul, interpreter for US forces for eleven years, resettled in Sacramento on a special visa. His wife and two daughters stay in Sacramento while he finds them a home here.
goals: A two-bedroom on Willow Lane for his family
Open a kebab counter at Greenleaf
Find out where his brother is
ambitions: A restaurant his daughters are embarrassed by
profile.social_preferences: Tea, chess, a long story told slowly.

secrets.truth: He sends money every month to a man in Peshawar who says he can get his brother out. He doesn't know if it's real.

social_media.bio: Greenleaf Market, evenings. Ask me for the good dates.

life_history: Taught English at a Kabul high school.
Eleven years as an interpreter for US forces.
Cashier at Greenleaf Market, evenings and Sundays.
